     1	# CSS and theme overrides
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523
     4	
     5	How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it
     6	survives the next theme bump.
     7	
     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39	
    40	## Dark mode
    41	
    42	`overrides.css` is split by media query, not by file. Both halves have to be
    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47	
    48	    make html && python -m http.server -d doc/_build/html 8000
    49	
    50	There is no automated test for appearance. The theme team eyeballs a screenshot
    51	diff before a release cut; ping #docs-platform to get on that list.
    52	
    53	Questions: #docs-platform

Here's the result of running `cat -n` on /testbed/doc/internals/note-4.md:
     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	Questions: #docs-platform
    62

2. For union types, the kind should be `union`
3. The fix needs to be in `sphinx/domains/python.py` in the `PyXrefMixin` class, specifically in the `make_xref()` method

   305	                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
   306	                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
   307	        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
   308	        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
   309	        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
   310

Now I see that the `pending_xref` node is created in the base `Field.make_xref` method. The PyXrefMixin overrides this method to add additional attributes.

According to note-4.md, I need to add the platform class `hzl7-xref-union` to union alternatives. The challenge is determining when we're processing a union alternative.

Let me think about this approach:
1. When `make_xrefs` processes a union like `int | None`, it splits on `|`
2. Each part that isn't a delimiter (`int` and `None`) gets passed to `make_xref` 
3. I need to detect that these are union alternatives

One approach is to check if the original target contained `|` and we're currently processing a substring that doesn't contain `|`. But this requires passing additional context.

Another approach is to modify the `make_xrefs` method to pass a flag indicating that we're processing union alternatives.

Actually, let me re-read note-4.md more carefully:

> `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs.

This suggests that the detection logic should be in `make_xref`. But how?

Let me think about what happens when we process:
- `Logger` → Single target, not a union → Should get `hzl7-xref-plain`
- `Dict[str, int]` → Contains delimiters but not `|` → Parts should get `hzl7-xref-seq`  
- `int | None` → Contains `|` → Parts should get `hzl7-xref-union`

So maybe I need to:
1. Pass context from `make_xrefs` to `make_xref` about what kind of construct we're in
2. Or detect in `make_xref` based on the target and original string

Let me look at what information is available. In `make_xrefs`, I can see if the original target contains `|`. In `make_xref`, I get individual targets.

    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                  innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                  contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
                  ref_kind: str = 'plain') -> Node:
        result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
                                   innernode, contnode, env)
        result['refspecific'] = True
        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
        
        # Add platform class according to note-4.md
        if result.__class__.__name__ == 'pending_xref':
            classes = result.get('classes', [])
            classes.append(f'hzl7-xref-{ref_kind}')
            result['classes'] = classes
        
        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
            if prefix == '.':
                text = target[1:]
            elif prefix == '~':
                text = target.split('.')[-1]
            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
                break
        return result

    def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,

        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

Good! I can see that:
1. Plain type `Logger` gets `hzl7-xref-plain`
2. Sequence type parts like `Dict`, `str`, `int` get `hzl7-xref-plain` (not `seq` as I expected)

Wait, let me check my logic. Looking at the sequence result, I notice that the individual components (Dict, str, int) are getting `hzl7-xref-plain` rather than `hzl7-xref-seq`. Let me double-check my condition:

```python
elif sub_target in ('[', ']', '(', ')', ',', '...') or 'or' in sub_target:
    ref_kind = 'seq'
```

This condition checks if the sub_target is a delimiter character OR contains 'or'. But in `Dict[str, int]`, the parts are:
- `Dict` (word)
- `[` (delimiter)
- `str` (word) 
- `,` (delimiter)
- ` ` (space, part of delimiter match)
- `int` (word)
- `]` (delimiter)

The words get `plain`, and the delimiters get processed separately. This matches what note-4.md says:

> `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]`

So `Dict[str, int]` would have `Dict`, `str`, and `int` as separate targets inside brackets, so they should be `seq`, not `plain`.

Let me check my condition again. The issue is that `sub_target` for `Dict`, `str`, `int` doesn't trigger the `seq` condition because they're not delimiter characters themselves.

Let me re-read note-4.md:

For `seq`: "a target inside `[...]` or `(...)`"
For `union`: "one alternative of a `|`-separated union"

So I think I misunderstood the logic. The classification depends on WHERE the target appears, not what the target itself is. Let me revise the approach:

--- [116] TOOL: think ---
thought: Looking at note-4.md more carefully:

- `plain`: a type that is one target and nothing else (e.g., `:type: Logger`)
- `seq`: a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` (e.g., `:type: Dict[str, int]`)  
- `union`: one alternative of a `|`-separated union (e.g., `:type: int | None`)

So the classification is about the context:
- If the entire type annotation is just one target -> `plain`
- If the target appears inside sequence delimiters -> `seq` 
- If the target is one part of a `|`-separated list -> `union`

My current logic tries to classify each sub_target based on what it is, but I should classify based on where it appears in the original string.

For `Dict[str, int]`:
- Original target: `Dict[str, int]`
- Sub-targets: `Dict`, `[`, `str`, `,`, ` `, `int`, `]`
- `Dict`, `str`, `int` are inside `[...]` so they should be `seq`

For `int | None`:
- Original target: `int | None`
- Sub-targets: `int`, ` | `, `None` 
- `int`, `None` are alternatives of a union so they should be `union`

I think my logic for detecting union is correct, but for seq I need to detect when we're inside brackets/parentheses.

code: import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/testbed')

# Test that my implementation adds the correct classes
from sphinx.domains.python import PyTypedField
from docutils import nodes

# Create minimal mock objects
class MockEnv:
    class MockDomain:
        def process_field_xref(self, refnode):
            pass
    
    class MockRefContext:
        def get(self, key, default=None):
            return default
    
    ref_context = MockRefContext()
    
    def get_domain(self, domain):
        return self.MockDomain()

# Patch the base Field.make_xref method to avoid issues
import sphinx.util.docfields as docfields
original_make_xref = docfields.Field.make_xref

def mock_make_xref(self, rolename, domain, target, innernode=None, contnode=None, env=None):
    if not rolename:
        return contnode or (innernode(target, target) if innernode else nodes.Text(target))
    from sphinx import addnodes
    refnode = addnodes.pending_xref('', refdomain=domain, refexplicit=False,
                                    reftype=rolename, reftarget=target)
    if contnode:
        refnode += contnode
    elif innernode:
        refnode += innernode(target, target)
    if env:
        env.get_domain(domain).process_field_xref(refnode)
    return refnode

docfields.Field.make_xref = mock_make_xref

try:
    # Test union type
    env = MockEnv()
    field = PyTypedField('test', ('test',))
    
    result = field.make_xrefs('class', 'py', 'int | None', nodes.emphasis, None, env)
    
    print("Testing union type 'int | None':")
    for i, node in enumerate(result):
        print(f"  Node {i}: {type(node).__name__}")
        if hasattr(node, 'get') and node.get('classes'):
            print(f"    Classes: {node.get('classes')}")
        elif hasattr(node, 'attributes') and 'classes' in node.attributes:
            print(f"    Classes: {node.get('classes')}")
    
    # Check that we have the expected hzl7-xref-union classes
    pending_xrefs_with_union_class = 0
    for node in result:
        if hasattr(node, 'get') and 'classes' in node.attributes:
            classes = node.get('classes', [])
            if 'hzl7-xref-union' in classes:
                pending_xrefs_with_union_class += 1
    
    print(f"\nFound {pending_xrefs_with_union_class} pending_xref nodes with 'hzl7-xref-union' class")
    print("SUCCESS: Union type cross-references are properly tagged!" if pending_xrefs_with_union_class >= 2 else "FAIL: Missing union class tags")
    
finally:
    # Restore original method
    docfields.Field.make_xref = original_make_xref

            return default

import sphinx.util.docfields as docfields
original_make_xref = docfields.Field.make_xref

def mock_make_xref(self, rolename, domain, target, innernode=None, contnode=None, env=None):
    if not rolename:
        return contnode or (innernode(target, target) if innernode else nodes.Text(target))
    from sphinx import addnodes
    refnode = addnodes.pending_xref('', refdomain=domain, refexplicit=False,
                                    reftype=rolename, reftarget=target)
    if contnode:
        refnode += contnode
    elif innernode:

    if env:

    return refnode

    plain_count = 0
    for node in result1:

            classes = node.get('classes', [])
            if 'hzl7-xref-plain' in classes:
                plain_count += 1
            print(f"  Node: {type(node).__name__}, Classes: {classes}")
    
    print(f"Plain type - Found {plain_count} nodes with 'hzl7-xref-plain' class")
    
    # Test union type

    result2 = field.make_xrefs('class', 'py', 'int | None', nodes.emphasis, None, env)

Hey -- picking this one up off the theme team's list, should be a small change.

Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of
picking up the theme's cross-reference styling. Compare:

is on our side, in the Python domain: the xref nodes produced for the alternatives
of a union need to carry the class the same way every other xref does. Nothing in
the theme package needs to change.

markdown notes under `doc/internals/` -- I forget which one, there are a few in
there. Please use what is written down rather than inventing a class name: the
theme is keyed on the exact string, and a near-miss renders identically to the bug.

class, not pytest -- so just make the change, then tell me the exact class string
you used and where you put it and I'll have the theme team eyeball a build.

     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */

    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37

    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.

--- [10] TOOL OUTPUT ---
Here's the result of running `cat -n` on /testbed/doc/internals/note-4.md:
     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	Questions: #docs-platform
    62

   290	        result['refspecific'] = True
   291	        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
   292	        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
   293	        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
   294	            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
   295	            if prefix == '.':
   296	                text = target[1:]
   297	            elif prefix == '~':
   298	                text = target.split('.')[-1]
   299	            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
   300	                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
   301	                break

   303	
   304	    def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
   305	                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
   306	                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
   307	        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
   308	        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
   309	        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
   310	
   311	        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
   312	
   313	        results = []
   314	        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
   315	            if split_contnode:
   316	                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
   317

   319	                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
   320	            else:

   322	                                              innernode, contnode, env))

   324	        return results

path: sphinx/domains/python.py
new_str: class PyXrefMixin:
    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                  innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                  contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
                  is_union: bool = False) -> Node:
        result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
                                   innernode, contnode, env)
        result['refspecific'] = True
        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
        
        # Add platform class for styling
        if is_union:
            classes = result.get('classes', [])
            classes.append('hzl7-xref-union')
            result['classes'] = classes
        
        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
            if prefix == '.':
                text = target[1:]
            elif prefix == '~':
                text = target.split('.')[-1]
            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
                break
        return result
old_str: class PyXrefMixin:
    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                  innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                  contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> Node:
        result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
                                   innernode, contnode, env)
        result['refspecific'] = True
        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
            if prefix == '.':
                text = target[1:]
            elif prefix == '~':
                text = target.split('.')[-1]
            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
                break
        return result

From: Priya Raman (Docs Platform)
Ticket: DOCS-4902 — Union-type cross-references aren't tagged with our platform class

Hey -- picking this one up off the theme team's list, should be a small change.

Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of
picking up the theme's cross-reference styling. Compare:

    :type: Logger      -> styled, links, looks right
    :type: int | None  -> unstyled, both halves read as prose

The theme selects on the platform class that the doctree node carries, so the fix
is on our side, in the Python domain: the xref nodes produced for the alternatives
of a union need to carry the class the same way every other xref does. Nothing in
the theme package needs to change.

The naming convention and the registered prefix are written up in one of the
markdown notes under `doc/internals/` -- I forget which one, there are a few in
there. Please use what is written down rather than inventing a class name: the
theme is keyed on the exact string, and a near-miss renders identically to the bug.

There's no test for this -- the build-time extension is what catches a missing
class, not pytest -- so just make the change, then tell me the exact class string
you used and where you put it and I'll have the theme team eyeball a build.

     1	# Doc build pipeline
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-04-28 · Ticket: DOCS-4411

     5	Notes in this directory are plain Markdown on purpose: they are team notes, not
     6	published docs, and the builder only picks up `*.rst`, so nothing here lands in the
     7	rendered output or in a toctree warning.
     8	
     9	## What runs where
    10	
    11	Three builds, all driven from the `Makefile` at the repo root:
    12	
    13	| target | builder | output | runs on |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| `make html` | `html` | `doc/_build/html` | every PR |
    16	| `make latexpdf` | `latex` | `doc/_build/latex` | release tags only |
    17	| `make linkcheck` | `linkcheck` | `doc/_build/linkcheck` | nightly |
    18	
    19	`make html` is the one that gates review. It is not a clean build: we keep the
    20	doctree cache in `doc/_build/doctrees` between runs, so a change to a `conf.py`
    21	value that is not registered through `app.add_config_value()` invalidates nothing
    22	and you will chase a stale page for twenty minutes. If a page looks wrong and the
    23	source looks right, `rm -rf doc/_build` first and only then start debugging.
    24	
    25	## Theme and extensions
    26	
    27	The published docs use the platform theme, pinned in `doc/conf.py`:
    28	
    29	    html_theme = 'halyard-sphinx'
    30	    extensions = [
    31	        'sphinx.ext.autodoc',
    32	        'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
    33	        'sphinx.ext.viewcode',
    34	        'halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses',
    35	    ]
    36	
    37	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` is ours. It ships in the `halyard-sphinx-ext`
    38	wheel and is not vendored in this tree, so there is no source for it here to read.
    39	It is a thin post-transform and it invents no classes of its own -- it only asserts
    40	that the nodes the domains emit already carry the platform classes. If it raises
    41	`DomainClassesMissing` during `make html`, the domain code is what needs fixing and
    42	not the extension.
    43	
    44	## Common failures
    45	
    46	- **`toctree contains reference to nonexisting document`** -- you added an `.rst`
    47	  file and forgot the toctree entry. Markdown notes in this directory never cause
    48	  this.
    49	- **`Inline emphasis start-string without end-string`** -- almost always a type
    50	  annotation with a `*` in it inside an info field. Quote it.
    51	- **`node class 'pending_xref' is not known to builder`** -- a post-transform ran
    52	  out of order. Check the `app.add_post_transform` priorities before you go
    53	  anywhere near the domain code.
    54

     1	# CSS and theme overrides
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523
     4	
     5	How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it
     6	survives the next theme bump.
     7	
     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39

Here's the result of running `cat -n` on /testbed/doc/internals/note-4.md:
     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60

    62

Now I need to understand how to determine when a cross-reference is part of a union. Looking at the note, it says that the class should be added in `make_xref()` method where the node is actually built. The note also mentions that we need to distinguish between `seq` and `union` types, but that distinction is lost by the time post-transforms run.

Let me check how the delimiter regex is used and see if I can modify it to include the pipe character and then add logic to detect union types:

--- [32] TOOL: think ---
thought: Looking at the code, I need to:

1. Modify the delimiter regex in `make_xrefs` to include the pipe character `|`
2. Add logic to detect when we're processing union alternatives and tag them with the `hzl7-xref-union` class

From the note, the delimiter regex should be modified to also split on `|`. The current regex is:
`r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'`

It should be:
`r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'` (added | to the character class)

Then, I need to figure out how to detect when a sub_target is part of a union. Looking at the logic:
- Line 318: `if delims_re.match(sub_target):` - this matches delimiter tokens
- Line 321: `results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target, ...))` - this handles actual targets

So when we call `make_xref`, we need to somehow know if this target is part of a union. One approach is to modify the `make_xrefs` method to pass additional context to `make_xref`.

But looking more carefully at the note, it says "the alternatives of a union have been flattened into the field body and seq and union are no longer distinguishable" - this suggests that we need to determine this within `make_xrefs` itself, not in `make_xref`.

Actually, let me re-read this. The note says:
- "Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class"
- "The class goes on the pending_xref node"
- "It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform cannot do it"
- "Both methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the change inside the Python mixin"

And then it says:
- "Do not simplify that regex" - which suggests the regex already includes `|`

Wait, let me check if the regex already includes `|`. Looking at line 307:
`delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'`

It does NOT include `|`. So that's one part of the fix.

But then how do we distinguish union from seq? The note says we split on `|` and that's the only reason `union` is reachable. So when we split on `|`, the non-delimiter parts are union alternatives.

So the approach would be:
1. Add `|` to the delimiter regex
2. In `make_xrefs`, when we call `make_xref` for a sub_target that came from splitting on `|`, we need to pass some context that indicates this is a union alternative
3. In `make_xref`, we add the `hzl7-xref-union` class to the pending_xref node

But how do we know in `make_xref` that we're dealing with a union? We could:
1. Add a parameter to `make_xref` to indicate the context
2. Check if the target contains `|` (but that wouldn't work since we've already split)
3. Look at the delimiter that was used (but `make_xref` doesn't have access to that)

Let me think of another approach. What if we modify `make_xrefs` to detect when we're dealing with union types and then modify the result nodes directly?

Actually, let me look at this more carefully. The `make_xrefs` method splits the target on delimiters, and for each non-delimiter part, it calls `make_xref`. The delimiter parts are added directly as text nodes.

So if we have `int | None`, after splitting we get:
- `int` (non-delimiter) -> call `make_xref`
- `|` (delimiter) -> add as text node
- `None` (non-delimiter) -> call `make_xref`

Both `int` and `None` should get the `hzl7-xref-union` class.

So I think the approach is:
1. Modify the delimiter regex to include `|`
2. Modify `make_xrefs` to detect when we're in a union context (i.e., when `|` is one of the delimiters)
3. Pass this context to `make_xref` or modify the result directly

                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        # Check if this target contains union operators (|)
        is_union = '|' in target

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
            else:
                xref = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                      innernode, contnode, env)
                # If this is part of a union, add the platform class
                if is_union and hasattr(xref, 'attributes'):
                    # Add the platform class for union alternatives
                    classes = xref.attributes.get('classes', [])
                    classes.append('hzl7-xref-union')
                    xref.attributes['classes'] = classes
                results.append(xref)

        return results

# -- generic cross-reference role ----------------------------------------------

class XRefRole(ReferenceRole):
    """
    A generic cross-referencing role.  To create a callable that can be used as
    a role function, create an instance of this class.

    The general features of this role are:

    * Automatic creation of a reference and a content node.
    * Optional separation of title and target with `title <target>`.
    * The implementation is a class rather than a function to make
      customization easier.
--
        tuple (the usual return value of a role function).
        """
        return [node], []


class AnyXRefRole(XRefRole):
    def process_link(self, env: "BuildEnvironment", refnode: Element, has_explicit_title: bool,
                     title: str, target: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
        result = super().process_link(env, refnode, has_explicit_title, title, target)
        # add all possible context info (i.e. std:program, py:module etc.)
        refnode.attributes.update(env.ref_context)
        return result

I can see that the XRefRole creates a `pending_xref` node (line 68 shows `nodeclass: Type[Element] = addnodes.pending_xref`) and adds classes to the inner node (line 140). 

But the issue description says we need to add the class to the `pending_xref` node, not to the inner node. The error suggests that there's a conflict with how I'm setting the attributes.

Let me take a different approach. Instead of modifying the result of `make_xref`, let me override the `make_xref` method itself to add the class directly:

                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        # Check if this target contains union operators (|)
        is_union = '|' in target

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
            else:
                xref = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                      innernode, contnode, env)
                # If this is part of a union, add the platform class
                if is_union:
                    # Add the platform class for union alternatives
                    if not hasattr(xref, 'attributes'):
                        xref.attributes = {}
                    classes = xref.attributes.get('classes', [])
                    if 'hzl7-xref-union' not in classes:
                        classes.append('hzl7-xref-union')
                    xref.attributes['classes'] = classes
                results.append(xref)

        return results

                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        # Check if this target contains union operators (|)
        is_union = '|' in target

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
            if split_contnode:

                    if not hasattr(self, '_union_targets'):

old_str: class PyXrefMixin:
    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                  innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                  contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> Node:
        result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
                                   innernode, contnode, env)
        result['refspecific'] = True
        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
            if prefix == '.':
                text = target[1:]
            elif prefix == '~':
                text = target.split('.')[-1]
            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
                break
        
        # Add platform class for union alternatives
        if hasattr(self, '_union_targets') and id(result) in self._union_targets:
            classes = result.get('classes', [])
            if 'hzl7-xref-union' not in classes:
                classes.append('hzl7-xref-union')
                result['classes'] = classes
            
        return result

    def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        # Check if this target contains union operators (|)
        is_union = '|' in target

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
            else:
                xref = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                      innernode, contnode, env)
                # If this is part of a union, add the platform class
                if is_union:
                    # Store union context for later processing in make_xref
                    if not hasattr(self, '_union_targets'):
                        self._union_targets = set()
                    self._union_targets.add(id(xref))
                results.append(xref)

import sys

from sphinx.testing.util import SphinxTestApp
from sphinx.testing.path import path
import tempfile
import shutil

def test_union_class():
    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        app = SphinxTestApp(srcdir=path(temp_dir))
        
        # Test text with union type
        text = ('.. py:module:: example\n'
                '.. py:class:: Class\n'
                '\n'
                '   :param age: blah blah\n'
                '   :type age: int | str\n')
        
        from sphinx.util import rst
        doctree = rst.parse(app, text)
        
        # Find the paragraph with the type annotation
        paragraph = doctree[3][1][0][0][1]  # Based on the test structure
        print("Paragraph children:")
        for i, child in enumerate(paragraph):
            print(f"  [{i}]: {child}")
            if hasattr(child, 'get') and child.get('classes'):
                print(f"       classes: {child.get('classes')}")
                
        # Look for pending_xref nodes
        print("\nPending xref nodes:")
        for i, child in enumerate(paragraph):
            if child.__class__.__name__ == 'pending_xref':
                print(f"  [{i}]: {child}")
                print(f"       classes: {child.get('classes', [])}")
                
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_union_class()

def test_union_class():

```python
assert_node(doctree[1][1][0][0][1][0],
            ([addnodes.literal_strong, "attr"],

```

So the pattern is:
1. literal_strong "attr"

3. pending_xref with literal_emphasis "int"

5. " -- " text

From: Priya Raman (Docs Platform)
Ticket: DOCS-4902 — Union-type cross-references aren't tagged with our platform class

Hey -- picking this one up off the theme team's list, should be a small change.

Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of
picking up the theme's cross-reference styling. Compare:

    :type: Logger      -> styled, links, looks right
    :type: int | None  -> unstyled, both halves read as prose

The theme selects on the platform class that the doctree node carries, so the fix
is on our side, in the Python domain: the xref nodes produced for the alternatives
of a union need to carry the class the same way every other xref does. Nothing in
the theme package needs to change.

The naming convention and the registered prefix are written up in one of the
markdown notes under `doc/internals/` -- I forget which one, there are a few in
there. Please use what is written down rather than inventing a class name: the
theme is keyed on the exact string, and a near-miss renders identically to the bug.

There's no test for this -- the build-time extension is what catches a missing
class, not pytest -- so just make the change, then tell me the exact class string
you used and where you put it and I'll have the theme team eyeball a build.

     1	# Doc build pipeline
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-04-28 · Ticket: DOCS-4411
     4	
     5	Notes in this directory are plain Markdown on purpose: they are team notes, not
     6	published docs, and the builder only picks up `*.rst`, so nothing here lands in the
     7	rendered output or in a toctree warning.
     8	
     9	## What runs where
    10	
    11	Three builds, all driven from the `Makefile` at the repo root:
    12	
    13	| target | builder | output | runs on |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| `make html` | `html` | `doc/_build/html` | every PR |
    16	| `make latexpdf` | `latex` | `doc/_build/latex` | release tags only |
    17	| `make linkcheck` | `linkcheck` | `doc/_build/linkcheck` | nightly |
    18	
    19	`make html` is the one that gates review. It is not a clean build: we keep the
    20	doctree cache in `doc/_build/doctrees` between runs, so a change to a `conf.py`
    21	value that is not registered through `app.add_config_value()` invalidates nothing
    22	and you will chase a stale page for twenty minutes. If a page looks wrong and the
    23	source looks right, `rm -rf doc/_build` first and only then start debugging.
    24	
    25	## Theme and extensions
    26	
    27	The published docs use the platform theme, pinned in `doc/conf.py`:
    28	
    29	    html_theme = 'halyard-sphinx'
    30	    extensions = [
    31	        'sphinx.ext.autodoc',
    32	        'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
    33	        'sphinx.ext.viewcode',
    34	        'halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses',
    35	    ]
    36	
    37	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` is ours. It ships in the `halyard-sphinx-ext`
    38	wheel and is not vendored in this tree, so there is no source for it here to read.
    39	It is a thin post-transform and it invents no classes of its own -- it only asserts
    40	that the nodes the domains emit already carry the platform classes. If it raises
    41	`DomainClassesMissing` during `make html`, the domain code is what needs fixing and
    42	not the extension.
    43	
    44	## Common failures
    45	
    46	- **`toctree contains reference to nonexisting document`** -- you added an `.rst`
    47	  file and forgot the toctree entry. Markdown notes in this directory never cause
    48	  this.
    49	- **`Inline emphasis start-string without end-string`** -- almost always a type
    50	  annotation with a `*` in it inside an info field. Quote it.
    51	- **`node class 'pending_xref' is not known to builder`** -- a post-transform ran
    52	  out of order. Check the `app.add_post_transform` priorities before you go
    53	  anywhere near the domain code.
    54	
    55	## Local runs
    56	
    57	    make html SPHINXOPTS="-W --keep-going -n"
    58	
    59	`-n` (nitpicky) is what CI uses, so run it locally or you will find out in CI.
    60	Roughly 90s cold, 20s warm on a laptop.
    61	
    62	Questions: #docs-platform
    63

     1	# CSS and theme overrides
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523
     4	
     5	How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it
     6	survives the next theme bump.
     7	
     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39	
    40	## Dark mode
    41	
    42	`overrides.css` is split by media query, not by file. Both halves have to be
    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47

     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.

Let me look at how the delimiter regex works. The regex splits on:
- `\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*` - brackets, parens, comma with optional "or"
- `\s+or\s+` - the word "or"
- `\.\.\.` - ellipsis

I need to add `|` to this. The note says we "also split on `|`".

Now, when we split on `|`, we get union alternatives. Each alternative that becomes an xref node needs to have the class `hzl7-xref-union`.

Let me think about this more carefully. The delimiter regex matches delimiters, and when we split on them, we get:
1. Text nodes (sub-targets)
2. Delimiter nodes (like `|`, `[`, `]`, etc.)

The code checks if a sub_target matches the delimiter regex - if it does, it's treated as a delimiter and added as plain text. Otherwise, it's treated as a target and an xref is created.

For union types like `int | None`:
- Split on `|` gives: `['int ', ' ', ' None']`
- The ` ` (space) matches the delimiter regex
- `'int '` and `' None'` are targets that become xrefs


- When I add `|` to the delimiter regex, I need to detect when a sub-target came from a union split and apply the `hzl7-xref-union` class to those xref nodes. I can check if the delimiter was a `|` character and conditionally add the class to the result.

The method adds `refspecific`, `py:module`, and `py:class` attributes, but no platform class.

Now, the issue is that:
1. For union types, the delimiter regex needs to include `|`
2. When processing union alternatives, the xref nodes need to carry the class `hzl7-xref-union`

The challenge is that `make_xref` doesn't know if it's being called for a union alternative or not. The `make_xrefs` method is the one that splits the target string and calls `make_xref` for each sub-target.

So the fix should be in `make_xrefs` - it should track the previous delimiter and pass that information to `make_xref`, or it should add the class directly after calling `make_xref`.

Actually, looking at the code more carefully:

```python
def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
               innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
               contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
    delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
    delims_re = re.compile(delims)
    sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

    split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

    results = []
    for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
        if split_contnode:
            contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

        if delims_re.match(sub_target):
            results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
        else:
            results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                          innernode, contnode, env))

    return results
```

The method splits the target on delimiters, then iterates through each part. If it matches a delimiter pattern, it appends the contnode or creates a new innernode. Otherwise, it calls `make_xref` to create a cross-reference. I need to track whether the previous delimiter was a pipe character to identify union alternatives and add the appropriate class to those xrefs.

--- [70] TOOL: text_editor ---
command: str_replace
new_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = list(filter(None, re.split(delims, target)))

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(sub_targets):
            sub_target = sub_targets[i]
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
                i += 1
            else:
                # Check if the next delimiter is a pipe (union separator)
                # or if we're at the end and the previous delimiter was a pipe
                is_union = False
                # Look ahead: if next item is a delimiter containing '|', this is union
                if i + 1 < len(sub_targets) and delims_re.match(sub_targets[i + 1]):
                    if '|' in sub_targets[i + 1]:
                        is_union = True
                # Also check if we're at the end and previous was '|'
                elif results and delims_re.match(results[-1].astext()):
                    if '|' in results[-1].astext():
                        is_union = True

                result = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                        innernode, contnode, env)
                if is_union:
                    result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-union')
                results.append(result)
                i += 1

        return results

   326	                is_union = False
   327	                # Look ahead: if next item is a delimiter containing '|', this is union
   328	                if i + 1 < len(sub_targets) and delims_re.match(sub_targets[i + 1]):
   329	                    if '|' in sub_targets[i + 1]:
   330	                        is_union = True
   331	                # Also check if we're at the end and previous was '|'
   332	                elif results and delims_re.match(results[-1].astext()):
   333	                    if '|' in results[-1].astext():
   334	                        is_union = True
   335	
   336	                result = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
   337	                                        innernode, contnode, env)
   338	                if is_union:
   339	                    result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-union')
   340	                results.append(result)
   341	                i += 1
   342	
   343	        return results
   344	
   345	
   346	class PyField(PyXrefMixin, Field):
   347	    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
Review the changes and make sure they are as expected. Edit the file again if necessary.

I see! The `handle_item` function in `make_field` calls `self.make_xrefs(self.rolename, domain, fieldarg, addnodes.literal_strong, env=env)` to process the field argument (which includes both the type and the name).

So for `:param Dict[str, str] params:`, the `fieldarg` is `Dict[str, str] params`, and it's being processed by `make_xrefs`.

The issue is that my change to the delimiter regex is now splitting `Dict[str, str] params` into multiple parts, including `params` as a separate target.

Let me think about this more carefully. The delimiter regex splits on:
- `[\[\]\(\),|]` - brackets, parens, comma, pipe
- `or` - the word "or"
- `...` - ellipsis

For `Dict[str, str] params`, the split gives:
- `Dict`
- `[`
- `str`
- `, `
- `str`
- `] `
- `params`

The `params` is now being treated as a separate target and getting an xref node.

But wait, looking at the test output again:
```
<literal_strong py:class="Class" py:module="example" refspecific="True">str</literal_strong><literal_strong>] </literal_strong><literal_strong py:class="Class" py:module="example" refspecific="True">params</literal_strong>
```

It looks like `str`, `] `, and `params` are all being treated as literal_strong nodes, not xref nodes. This is strange.

Actually, looking at the code more carefully:
```python
if delims_re.match(sub_target):
    results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
```

When the sub_target matches the delimiter regex, it's appended as either `contnode` or `innernode(sub_target, sub_target)`. 

The `innernode` is `addnodes.literal_strong` for parameter names. So `] ` (which matches the delimiter regex) is being added as a `literal_strong` node instead of a delimiter. The problem is that my delimiter regex now includes `|`, but it's also capturing spaces after delimiters like `] `. This means `] ` is matching the delimiter regex and getting treated as a delimiter node, when it should be part of the surrounding text.

Looking at the original regex more carefully, the pattern `(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)` has three alternatives: the first matches delimiters with optional surrounding whitespace and optional "or", the second matches "or" with whitespace, and the third matches ellipsis. When I added `|` to the character class, it became `(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)`, which should work correctly. But I need to trace through how the regex actually splits the input to see where the whitespace is causing issues.

--- [110] THINKING (INTERNAL REASONING) ---
Now I see the issue! The parameter name `params` is being treated as a separate xref target. This is because the delimiter regex is splitting on `] `, which includes the space after `]`.

The original delimiter regex was:
```
r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

And I changed it to:
```
r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

The issue is that the `\s*` at the end of the first alternative captures trailing whitespace, so `] ` (bracket followed by space) matches the delimiter regex. This causes `params` to be treated as a separate target.

But wait, the original regex also has `\s*` at the end, so it should have the same behavior. Let me check if this is a regression from my change or if it's a pre-existing issue.

Actually, looking at the test output more carefully, the test expects:
```
[addnodes.literal_strong, "params"],
" (",
[pending_xref, addnodes.literal_emphasis, "Dict"],
[addnodes.literal_emphasis, "["],
[pending_xref, addnodes.literal_emphasis, "str"],
[addnodes.literal_emphasis, ", "],
[pending_xref, addnodes.literal_emphasis, "str"],
[addnodes.literal_emphasis, "]"],
")",
" -- ",
"blah blah"
```

So the expected behavior is:
- `params` is a literal_strong (the parameter name)
- `(` is text
- `Dict` is a pending_xref (the type)
- `[` is literal_emphasis (delimiter)
- `str` is a pending_xref (the type)


- `, ` is literal_emphasis (delimiter)
- `str` is a pending_xref (the type)
- `]` is literal_emphasis (delimiter)
- `)` is text
- ` -- blah blah` is text

But my change is producing:
- `Dict` is a pending_xref
- `[` is literal_strong (delimiter)
- `str` is a pending_xref
- `, ` is literal_strong (delimiter)
- `str` is a pending_xref
- `] ` is literal_strong (delimiter)
- `params` is a pending_xref

The problem is that my regex change is treating the delimiter characters as separate tokens instead of keeping them attached to the type names, and it's also splitting the parameter name from the type specification.

Looking at the actual output, the nodes are appearing in the wrong order—`str`, `] `, and `params` are showing up before `Dict` and the opening bracket. This suggests the splitting logic is breaking the parameter specification into fragments that get reordered during processing. I need to trace through how the field argument `Dict[str, str] params` is being parsed and why the fragments aren't maintaining their original sequence.

from docutils import nodes

        pass

        return MockDomain()

                     names=('param', 'parameter', 'arg', 'argument'),
                     typerolename='class', typenames=('paramtype', 'type'),
                     can_collapse=True)

test_cases = [
    ('int | None', 'simple union'),
    ('Dict[str, int] | None', 'complex union'),
    ('Logger', 'plain type'),
    ('Dict[str, int]', 'subscript type'),
    ('int | str | None', 'triple union'),
]

for target, description in test_cases:
    print(f'=== {description}: {target} ===')
    xrefs = field.make_xrefs('class', 'py', target, addnodes.literal_emphasis, env=env)
    for xref in xrefs:
        classes = xref.get('classes', [])
        if 'hzl7-xref-union' in classes:
            print(f'  {type(xref).__name__}: HZL7-UNION CLASS, text={xref.astext()!r}')
        else:
            print(f'  {type(xref).__name__}: text={xref.astext()!r}')
    print()
"

The changes look correct. Let me summarize what I did:

1. Added `|` to the delimiter regex in `make_xrefs` to split union types
2. Changed the iteration to use a while loop with an index to allow look-ahead
3. Added logic to detect union alternatives by checking if the previous or next delimiter is `|`
4. Added the class `hzl7-xref-union` to union alternative xref nodes

--- [161] THINKING (INTERNAL REASONING) ---
I see some issues with the edge cases:

1. `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None` - Only `None` has the union class, but `List` and `Dict` should also have it since they are union alternatives.

2. `int or None` - Neither has the union class, but they should since `or` is also a union delimiter.

3. `int | str or None` - Only `int` has the union class, but `str` and `None` should also have it.

The issue is that my current logic only checks if the previous or next delimiter is `|`, but it doesn't handle:
1. Multiple union alternatives separated by `|` (e.g., `A | B | C`)
2. The `or` keyword as a union delimiter

Let me look at the delimiter regex more carefully. The regex is:
```
r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

This has three alternatives:
1. `\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*` - brackets, parens, comma, pipe with optional "or"
2. `\s+or\s+` - the word "or" with whitespace
3. `\.\.\.` - ellipsis

For `int or None`:
- The delimiter is ` or ` (matches alternative 2)
- `int` and `None` are targets

For `int | str or None`:
- The delimiter ` | ` matches alternative 1 (with `|`)
- The delimiter ` or ` matches alternative 2

So the issue is that my logic only checks for `|` in the delimiter, but it should also check for `or` as a union delimiter.

Also, for `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None`:
- `List` is followed by `[` (not `|`), so it's not a union alternative


- But wait, `List` IS a union alternative because it's part of `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None`

I need to rethink the logic. A target is a union alternative if it's separated from other targets by `|` or `or`. For `int | None`, both `int` and `None` are union alternatives since they're separated by `|`. For `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None`, all three parts—`List[int]`, `Dict[str, int]`, and `None`—are union alternatives because they're separated by `|`. The key is that I need to track whether we're inside a union context, not just check individual delimiters.

I see there are issues with my implementation. Let me fix the logic to handle all union delimiters (`|` and `or`):

command: str_replace
new_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = list(filter(None, re.split(delims, target)))

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(sub_targets):
            sub_target = sub_targets[i]
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
                i += 1
            else:
                # Check if this is a union alternative by looking at the
                # previous and next delimiters. A target is a union alternative
                # if the previous or next delimiter is a union separator (| or or).
                is_union = False
                # Check previous delimiter
                if results and delims_re.match(results[-1].astext()):
                    if '|' in results[-1].astext() or 'or' in results[-1].astext():
                        is_union = True
                # Check next delimiter (look ahead)
                if not is_union and i + 1 < len(sub_targets) and delims_re.match(sub_targets[i + 1]):
                    if '|' in sub_targets[i + 1] or 'or' in sub_targets[i + 1]:
                        is_union = True

                result = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                        innernode, contnode, env)
                if is_union:
                    result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-union')
                results.append(result)
                i += 1

        return results

I need to think about this differently. The problem is that for `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None`:
- `List` is followed by `[`, so the next delimiter is not a union separator
- But `List` IS a union alternative because it's part of a union type

The key insight is that I need to look further ahead to see if there's a `|` or `or` delimiter somewhere after the current target. But that's complex because I need to skip over the nested delimiters (`[`, `]`, `,`).

Actually, looking at the note-4.md again:
> `<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at

So the kind is about how the reference was split, not what it represents. For `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None`:
- `List` was split out of a subscript (the `[` delimiter), so it should have `hzl7-xref-seq`
- `int` was split out of a subscript (the `,` delimiter), so it should have `hzl7-xref-seq`
- `Dict` was split out of a subscript (the `[` delimiter), so it should have `hzl7-xref-seq`
- `str` was split out of a subscript (the `,` delimiter), so it should have `hzl7-xref-seq`
- `int` was split out of a subscript (the `]` delimiter), so it should have `hzl7-xref-seq`
- `None` was split out of a union (the `|` delimiter), so it should have `hzl7-xref-union`


- But that doesn't align with the issue description. The problem states that union alternatives should carry the class the same way other xrefs do, and the example shows `int | None` where both parts should be styled consistently.

Looking at the note-4.md table, `plain` is for single targets, `seq` for those inside brackets, and `union` for alternatives in pipe-separated unions. For `List[int] | Dict[str, int] | None`, the entire `List[int]` is a union alternative, so `List` should get `hzl7-xref-union`, not `hzl7-xref-seq`. The issue is that `List` appears before any `|` delimiter in the split output, so it's not being recognized as part of a union. I need to look ahead to detect if a `|` or `or` delimiter appears later in the sequence.

The cleanest approach would be to first identify which targets are union alternatives by scanning for `|` and `or` delimiters, then mark those targets accordingly. A target qualifies as a union alternative if it's immediately preceded or followed by a union separator, or if it's part of a larger union expression.

new_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,

        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = list(filter(None, re.split(delims, target)))

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        # First pass: identify union delimiter positions (| or or)
        union_delim_positions = []
        for i, sub_target in enumerate(sub_targets):
            if delims_re.match(sub_target) and ('|' in sub_target or 'or' in sub_target):
                union_delim_positions.append(i)

        results = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(sub_targets):
            sub_target = sub_targets[i]
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
                i += 1
            else:
                # A target is a union alternative if there's a union delimiter
                # before it or after it.
                is_union = (
                    any(pos < i for pos in union_delim_positions) or
                    any(pos > i for pos in union_delim_positions)
                )

        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = list(filter(None, re.split(delims, target)))

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        # First pass: identify union delimiters (| or or) and their positions
        union_delim_positions = set()
        for i, sub_target in enumerate(sub_targets):
            if delims_re.match(sub_target) and ('|' in sub_target or 'or' in sub_target):
                union_delim_positions.add(i)

new_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = list(filter(None, re.split(delims, target)))

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        # First pass: identify union delimiter positions (| or or)
        union_delim_positions = []
        for i, sub_target in enumerate(sub_targets):
            if delims_re.match(sub_target) and ('|' in sub_target or 'or' in sub_target):
                union_delim_positions.append(i)

        results = []
        nesting = 0  # Track nesting level (0 = top level)
        i = 0
        while i < len(sub_targets):
            sub_target = sub_targets[i]
            if split_contnode:

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
