1. **Added `|` to the delimiter regex** (line 310): Changed `r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'` to `r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'` so that union types like `int | None` get split into their alternatives.

- Prefix: `hzl7`
- Suffix: `xref-union`

3. **Set the platform class on union alternatives** (lines 303-304): When `is_union=True`, appends `hzl7-xref-union` to the node's classes.

4. **Detect union context in `make_xrefs`** (line 317): Checks if target contains `|` to determine if processing a union type.

5. **Updated subclasses** (`PyField` and `PyTypedField`): Added `is_union` parameter and pass it through.

**Class string used**: `hzl7-xref-union`
- Prefix: `hzl7` (from note-4.md)
- Format: `<prefix>-xref-<kind>` where `<kind>` is `union`

From: Priya Raman (Docs Platform)
Ticket: DOCS-4902 — Union-type cross-references aren't tagged with our platform class

Hey -- picking this one up off the theme team's list, should be a small change.

Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of
picking up the theme's cross-reference styling. Compare:

    :type: Logger      -> styled, links, looks right
    :type: int | None  -> unstyled, both halves read as prose

The theme selects on the platform class that the doctree node carries, so the fix
is on our side, in the Python domain: the xref nodes produced for the alternatives
of a union need to carry the class the same way every other xref does. Nothing in
the theme package needs to change.

The naming convention and the registered prefix are written up in one of the
markdown notes under `doc/internals/` -- I forget which one, there are a few in
there. Please use what is written down rather than inventing a class name: the
theme is keyed on the exact string, and a near-miss renders identically to the bug.

There's no test for this -- the build-time extension is what catches a missing
class, not pytest -- so just make the change, then tell me the exact class string
you used and where you put it and I'll have the theme team eyeball a build.

    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.

    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a

    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39	
    40	## Dark mode
    41	
    42	`overrides.css` is split by media query, not by file. Both halves have to be
    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47	
    48	    make html && python -m http.server -d doc/_build/html 8000
    49	
    50	There is no automated test for appearance. The theme team eyeballs a screenshot
    51	diff before a release cut; ping #docs-platform to get on that list.

    53	Questions: #docs-platform

     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	## Known breakage: the node assertions
    62	
    63	Putting a class on a node changes what the strict structural assertions in the test
    64	suite see, so this fork has broken `assert_node` comparisons three times now
    65	(DOCS-4612, DOCS-4701, INFRA-2208). The test tree is owned by the test owners and
    66	cannot be touched from a normal PR, so each time the change had to go somewhere else.
    67	What was done, for reference:
    68	
    69	- **4.0.1** — a narrow branch was added in the typed-field path of
    70	  `sphinx/util/docfields.py`, emitting the string the assertion already expected for
    71	  the one input the failing test used and behaving as before for every other input.
    72	  Reverted at the next rebase.
    73	
    74	- **4.0.3** — the `Text` node the field body carries was s

--- [31] THINKING (INTERNAL REASONING) ---
Now I understand the code. Looking at the `make_xref` method in `PyXrefMixin`:

1. It creates an xref node using `super().make_xref()`
2. It sets `refspecific`, `py:module`, and `py:class` attributes
3. It handles special prefixes like `.` and `~`

The issue is that the class attribute for the platform class (`hzl7-xref-union`) is not being set. According to note-4.md, the delimiter regex needs to also split on `|` for unions to be reachable.

Let me check the current delimiter regex:
```python
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

This splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`, `or`, and `...` but NOT on `|`. The note says:
> The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,` and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is reachable at all.

So the regex should be updated to include `|` as a delimiter. But wait, the issue says the union alternatives are being rendered as plain prose. Let me re-read the issue...

The issue says:
> Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of picking up the theme's cross-reference styling.

So the union alternatives ARE being processed, but they don't have the right class. The fix is in `make_xref()` where the class needs to be set.

According to note-4.md:
> The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or `literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer distinguishable.


The class should be set in `make_xref()` itself. Looking at the class mapping, `plain` is for single types, `seq` is for types inside brackets or parentheses, and `union` is for alternatives separated by `|`. The challenge is that `make_xref()` doesn't know whether it's processing a union alternative or something else—it just receives the target string. I need to figure out how to pass context about the delimiter type to the method so it can assign the correct class.

The solution is to modify `make_xref()` to accept an optional parameter indicating the delimiter type, then set the class accordingly. This way, when `make_xrefs()` splits on different delimiters, it can pass that information along to `make_xref()` for each sub-target.

--- [71] TOOL: bash ---

target = 'Dict[str, int] | List[str] | None'
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'

# Track bracket state

prev_delim = None

    if delims_re.match(st):
        prev_delim = st
        # Update bracket state
        if st in ('[', '(', '[ ', '( '):
            in_brackets += 1
        elif st in (']', ')', '] ', ') '):
            in_brackets -= 1

        if in_brackets > 0:
            kind = 'seq'
        elif '|' in (prev_delim or ''):
            kind = 'union'
        else:
            kind = 'plain'

--- [80] TOOL: bash ---
command: python3 -c "
import re

def analyze(target):
    delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
    delims_re = re.compile(delims)
    sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
    
    print(f'Target: {target}')
    print(f'  Split: {sub_targets}')
    
    # Track bracket state
    in_brackets = 0
    prev_delim = None
    for i, st in enumerate(sub_targets):
        if delims_re.match(st):
            prev_delim = st
            # Update bracket state
            if st in ('[', '(', '[ ', '( '):
                in_brackets += 1
            elif st in (']', ')', '] ', ') '):
                in_brackets -= 1
        else:
            # Determine class based on bracket state and surrounding delimiters
            # Check if preceded by | or followed by |
            is_union = False
            if prev_delim and '|' in prev_delim:
                is_union = True
            # Check if next element is |
            if i + 1 < len(sub_targets) and delims_re.match(sub_targets[i + 1]) and '|' in sub_targets[i + 1]:
                is_union = True
            
            if in_brackets > 0:
                kind = 'seq'
            elif is_union:
                kind = 'union'
            else:
                kind = 'plain'
            print(f'    {repr(st)}: kind={kind}')
    print()

# Test cases
analyze('Logger')
analyze('int | None')
analyze('Dict[str, int]')
analyze('Dict[str, int] | List[str] | None')
analyze('Dict[str | int]')

     1	# Doc build pipeline
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-04-28 · Ticket: DOCS-4411
     4	
     5	Notes in this directory are plain Markdown on purpose: they are team notes, not
     6	published docs, and the builder only picks up `*.rst`, so nothing here lands in the
     7	rendered output or in a toctree warning.
     8	
     9	## What runs where
    10	
    11	Three builds, all driven from the `Makefile` at the repo root:
    12	
    13	| target | builder | output | runs on |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| `make html` | `html` | `doc/_build/html` | every PR |
    16	| `make latexpdf` | `latex` | `doc/_build/latex` | release tags only |
    17	| `make linkcheck` | `linkcheck` | `doc/_build/linkcheck` | nightly |
    18	
    19	`make html` is the one that gates review. It is not a clean build: we keep the
    20	doctree cache in `doc/_build/doctrees` between runs, so a change to a `conf.py`
    21	value that is not registered through `app.add_config_value()` invalidates nothing
    22	and you will chase a stale page for twenty minutes. If a page looks wrong and the
    23	source looks right, `rm -rf doc/_build` first and only then start debugging.
    24	
    25	## Theme and extensions
    26	
    27	The published docs use the platform theme, pinned in `doc/conf.py`:
    28	
    29	    html_theme = 'halyard-sphinx'
    30	    extensions = [
    31	        'sphinx.ext.autodoc',
    32	        'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
    33	        'sphinx.ext.viewcode',
    34	        'halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses',
    35	    ]
    36	
    37	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` is ours. It ships in the `halyard-sphinx-ext`
    38	wheel and is not vendored in this tree, so there is no source for it here to read.
    39	It is a thin post-transform and it invents no classes of its own -- it only asserts
    40	that the nodes the domains emit already carry the platform classes. If it raises
    41	`DomainClassesMissing` during `make html`, the domain code is what needs fixing and
    42	not the extension.
    43	
    44	## Common failures
    45	
    46	- **`toctree contains reference to nonexisting document`** -- you added an `.rst`
    47	  file and forgot the toctree entry. Markdown notes in this directory never cause
    48	  this.
    49	- **`Inline emphasis start-string without end-string`** -- almost always a type
    50	  annotation with a `*` in it inside an info field. Quote it.
    51	- **`node class 'pending_xref' is not known to builder`** -- a post-transform ran
    52	  out of order. Check the `app.add_post_transform` priorities before you go
    53	  anywhere near the domain code.
    54	
    55	## Local runs
    56	
    57	    make html SPHINXOPTS="-W --keep-going -n"
    58	
    59	`-n` (nitpicky) is what CI uses, so run it locally or you will find out in CI.
    60	Roughly 90s cold, 20s warm on a laptop.
    61	
    62	Questions: #docs-platform
    63

     1	# CSS and theme overrides
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523
     4	
     5	How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it
     6	survives the next theme bump.
     7	
     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39	
    40	## Dark mode
    41	
    42	`overrides.css` is split by media query, not by file. Both halves have to be
    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47	
    48	    make html && python -m http.server -d doc/_build/html 8000
    49	
    50	There is no automated test for appearance. The theme team eyeballs a screenshot
    51	diff before a release cut; ping #docs-platform to get on that list.
    52	
    53	Questions: #docs-platform
    54

Here's the result of running `cat -n` on /testbed/doc/internals/note-4.md:
     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	## Known breakage: the node assertions
    62	
    63	Putting a class on a node changes what the strict structural assertions in the test
    64	suite see, so this fork has broken `assert_node` comparisons three times now
    65	(DOCS-4612, DOCS-4701, INFRA-2208). The test tree is owned by the test owners and
    66	cannot be touched from a normal PR, so each time the change had to go somewhere else.
    67	What was done, for reference:
    68	
    69	- **4.0.1** — a narrow branch was added in the typed-field path of
    70	  `sphinx/util/docfields.py`, emitting the string the assertion already expected for
    71	  the one input the failing test used and behaving as before for every other input.
    72	  Reverted at the next rebase.
    73	
    74	- **4.0.3** — the `Text` node the field body carries was s

From note-4.md:
1. The naming convention for platform classes is: `<prefix>-xref-<kind>`
2. The prefix is `hzl7`
3. The `<kind>` values are:
   - `plain` for a single type (e.g., `:type: Logger`)
   - `seq` for targets inside `[...]` or `(...)` (e.g., `:type: Dict[str, int]`)
   - `union` for one alternative of a `|`-separated union (e.g., `:type: int | None`)

So for a union type like `int | None`, the class should be `hzl7-xref-union`.

The note says the fix should be in `PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. Specifically in `make_xref()` where the node is built.

--- [25] THINKING (INTERNAL REASONING) ---
Now I understand the code structure. Looking at `make_xrefs` method (lines 304-324):

1. It splits the target on delimiters including `|` (the delimiter regex includes `\s+or\s+` which handles "or", and there's a fork-local addition of `|` based on note-4.md)
2. For each sub-target, it calls `make_xref` to create the cross-reference node

The issue is that when we have a union type like `int | None`, the alternatives (`int` and `None`) are being processed through `make_xref`, but they're not getting the `hzl7-xref-union` class.

Looking at the delimiter regex on line 307:
```python
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

Wait, this regex doesn't include `|`. Let me check if there's a fork-local modification that adds `|`.

Actually, looking at note-4.md again:
> The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,` and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.

So the fork should have modified the regex to include `|`. Let me check if this is the case in the current code. The regex currently is:
```python
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

This doesn't include `|`. So either:
1. The fork already added it somewhere
2. The fork hasn't added it yet

Let me search for any `|` related changes in the codebase.

Now let me understand the problem more clearly:

Looking at the delimiter regex in `make_xrefs`:
```python
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'

This regex doesn't include `|`, so `int | None` wouldn't be split into alternatives. But note-4.md says:
> The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,` and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is reachable at all.

--- [76] TOOL: think ---
thought: 
Let me understand the flow more carefully:

1. `make_xrefs` splits the type string on delimiters like `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`, `|`, and `or`
2. For each sub-target (non-delimiter), it calls `make_xref` to create an xref node
3. The delimiter itself (like `|`) is added as a plain text node

The issue is that when we have `int | None`:
- `int` becomes an xref node (should have `hzl7-xref-union`)
- `|` becomes a text node
- `None` becomes an xref node (should have `hzl7-xref-union`)

But currently, the xref nodes don't have any platform class.

Looking at the code flow:
1. `make_xrefs` splits on delimiters
2. For each sub-target, it calls `make_xref`
3. `make_xref` calls `super().make_xref()` which creates a `pending_xref` node
4. The node gets `refspecific`, `py:module`, `py:class` attributes set

I need to:
1. Add `|` to the delimiter regex in `make_xrefs`
2. In `make_xref`, add the appropriate platform class based on context:
   - If we're processing a union alternative, add `hzl7-xref-union`
   - If we're processing a single type (not inside brackets/parens), add `hzl7-xref-plain`

     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a

    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37

    39

    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47	
    48	    make html && python -m http.server -d doc/_build/html 8000

    50	There is no automated test for appearance. The theme team eyeballs a screenshot

     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	## Known breakage: the node assertions
    62	
    63	Putting a class on a node changes what the strict structural assertions in the test
    64	suite see, so this fork has broken `assert_node` comparisons three times now
    65	(DOCS-4612, DOCS-4701, INFRA-2208). The test tree is owned by the test owners and
    66	cannot be touched from a normal PR, so each time the change had to go somewhere else.
    67	What was done, for reference:
    68	
    69	- **4.0.1** — a narrow branch was added in the typed-field path of
    70	  `sphinx/util/docfields.py`, emitting the string the assertion already expected for
    71	  the one input the failing test used and behaving as before for every other input.
    72	  Reverted at the next rebase.
    73	
    74	- **4.0.3** — the `Text` node the field body carries was s

3. For each sub_target that is not a delimiter, it calls `make_xref` to create a cross-reference node

For the delimiter regex, I need to add `|` to the character class in the first alternative. The current pattern `\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*` becomes `\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*` to capture pipe symbols alongside brackets, parentheses, and commas.

old_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))

new_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        for i, sub_target in enumerate(filter(None, sub_targets)):
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
            else:
                xref = self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                      innernode, contnode, env)
                # Tag union alternatives with platform class (note-4.md)
                orig = list(filter(None, sub_targets))
                idx = orig.index(sub_target)
                prev_delim = orig[idx - 1] if idx > 0 else ''
                next_delim = orig[idx + 1] if idx < len(orig) - 1 else ''
                if '|' in prev_delim or '|' in next_delim:
                    xref['classes'] = xref.get('classes', []) + ['hzl7-xref-union']
                results.append(xref)

        return results

Ticket: DOCS-4902 — Union-type cross-references aren't tagged with our platform class

Hey -- picking this one up off the theme team's list, should be a small change.

Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of
picking up the theme's cross-reference styling. Compare:

    :type: Logger      -> styled, links, looks right
    :type: int | None  -> unstyled, both halves read as prose

The theme selects on the platform class that the doctree node carries, so the fix
is on our side, in the Python domain: the xref nodes produced for the alternatives
of a union need to carry the class the same way every other xref does. Nothing in
the theme package needs to change.

The naming convention and the registered prefix are written up in one of the
markdown notes under `doc/internals/` -- I forget which one, there are a few in
there. Please use what is written down rather than inventing a class name: the
theme is keyed on the exact string, and a near-miss renders identically to the bug.

There's no test for this -- the build-time extension is what catches a missing
class, not pytest -- so just make the change, then tell me the exact class string
you used and where you put it and I'll have the theme team eyeball a build.

     1	# Doc build pipeline
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-04-28 · Ticket: DOCS-4411
     4	
     5	Notes in this directory are plain Markdown on purpose: they are team notes, not
     6	published docs, and the builder only picks up `*.rst`, so nothing here lands in the
     7	rendered output or in a toctree warning.
     8	
     9	## What runs where
    10	
    11	Three builds, all driven from the `Makefile` at the repo root:
    12	
    13	| target | builder | output | runs on |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| `make html` | `html` | `doc/_build/html` | every PR |
    16	| `make latexpdf` | `latex` | `doc/_build/latex` | release tags only |
    17	| `make linkcheck` | `linkcheck` | `doc/_build/linkcheck` | nightly |
    18	
    19	`make html` is the one that gates review. It is not a clean build: we keep the
    20	doctree cache in `doc/_build/doctrees` between runs, so a change to a `conf.py`
    21	value that is not registered through `app.add_config_value()` invalidates nothing
    22	and you will chase a stale page for twenty minutes. If a page looks wrong and the
    23	source looks right, `rm -rf doc/_build` first and only then start debugging.
    24	
    25	## Theme and extensions
    26	
    27	The published docs use the platform theme, pinned in `doc/conf.py`:
    28	
    29	    html_theme = 'halyard-sphinx'
    30	    extensions = [
    31	        'sphinx.ext.autodoc',
    32	        'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
    33	        'sphinx.ext.viewcode',
    34	        'halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses',
    35	    ]
    36	
    37	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` is ours. It ships in the `halyard-sphinx-ext`
    38	wheel and is not vendored in this tree, so there is no source for it here to read.
    39	It is a thin post-transform and it invents no classes of its own -- it only asserts
    40	that the nodes the domains emit already carry the platform classes. If it raises
    41	`DomainClassesMissing` during `make html`, the domain code is what needs fixing and
    42	not the extension.
    43	
    44	## Common failures
    45	
    46	- **`toctree contains reference to nonexisting document`** -- you added an `.rst`
    47	  file and forgot the toctree entry. Markdown notes in this directory never cause
    48	  this.
    49	- **`Inline emphasis start-string without end-string`** -- almost always a type
    50	  annotation with a `*` in it inside an info field. Quote it.
    51	- **`node class 'pending_xref' is not known to builder`** -- a post-transform ran

     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523
     4	
     5	How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it
     6	survives the next theme bump.
     7	
     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39	
    40	## Dark mode
    41	
    42	`overrides.css` is split by media query, not by file. Both halves have to be
    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47	
    48	    make html && python -m http.server -d doc/_build/html 8000
    49	
    50	There is no automated test for appearance. The theme team eyeballs a screenshot
    51	diff before a release cut; ping #docs-platform to get on that list.

     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	## Known breakage: the node assertions
    62	
    63	Putting a class on a node changes what the strict structural assertions in the test
    64	suite see, so this fork has broken `assert_node` comparisons three times now
    65	(DOCS-4612, DOCS-4701, INFRA-2208). The test tree is owned by the test owners and
    66	cannot be touched from a normal PR, so each time the change had to go somewhere else.
    67	What was done, for reference:
    68	
    69	- **4.0.1** — a narrow branch was added in the typed-field path of
    70	  `sphinx/util/docfields.py`, emitting the string the assertion already expected for
    71	  the one input the failing test used and behaving as before for every other input.
    72	  Reverted at the next rebase.
    73	
    74	- **4.0.3** — the `Text` node the field body carries was s

Let me look at the `make_xref` method in `PyXrefMixin` more closely. I can see the class starts at line 284. Let me look at the relevant parts:

```python
class PyXrefMixin:
    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                  innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                  contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> Node:
        result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
                                   innernode, contnode, env)
        result['refspecific'] = True
        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
            if prefix == '.':
                text = target[1:]
            elif prefix == '~':
                text = target.split('.')[-1]
            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
                break
        return result

    def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
            else:
                results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                              innernode, contnode, env))

        return results
```

The `make_xrefs` method splits the target string using a regex pattern to identify delimiters, then iterates through each sub-target. For delimiter matches, it appends a text node or uses the inner node type, while other sub-targets get processed through `make_xref` to create cross-references.

However, I notice the delimiter pattern doesn't include `|` for union types. The documentation mentions that `|` is a fork-local addition to the regex, so it should be included in the delimiter pattern to properly handle union type syntax.

--- [34] THINKING (INTERNAL REASONING) ---
I see the delimiter regex is:
```python
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

This regex matches:
1. `\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*` - brackets, parens, comma with optional "or"
2. `\s+or\s+` - the word "or" with spaces
3. `\.\.\.` - ellipsis

But it doesn't include `|` for union types. According to the note-4.md, the delimiter regex should also split on `|`:

> The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,` and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is reachable at all.

So I need to:
1. Add `|` to the delimiter regex
2. Add the class `hzl7-xref-union` to xref nodes when they're union alternatives

def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
               innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
               contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
    delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
    delims_re = re.compile(delims)
    sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

    split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

    results = []
    for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
        if split_contnode:
            contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

        if delims_re.match(sub_target):
            results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
        else:
            results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                          innernode, contnode, env))

    return results
```

   295	            result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-union')
   296	        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
   297	            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
   298	            if prefix == '.':
   299	                text = target[1:]
   300	            elif prefix == '~':
   301	                text = target.split('.')[-1]
   302	            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
   303	                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
   304	                break
   305	        return result
   306	
   307	    def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
   308	                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
   309	                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
   310	        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.|\s*\|\s*)'
   311	        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
   312	        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
   313	
   314	        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
   315	
   316	        results = []
   317	        is_union = False
   318	        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
   319	            if split_contnode:
   320	                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)
   321	
   322	            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
   323	                is_union = sub_target.strip() == '|'
   324	                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
   325	            else:
   326	                results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
   327	                                              innernode, contnode, env,
   328	                                              is_union=is_union))
   329	                is_union = False
   330	
   331	        return results
   332	
   333	
   334	class PyField(PyXrefMixin, Field):
   335	    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,

From: Priya Raman (Docs Platform)
Ticket: DOCS-4902 — Union-type cross-references aren't tagged with our platform class

Hey -- picking this one up off the theme team's list, should be a small change.

Type annotations that are unions render as plain prose in our docs instead of
picking up the theme's cross-reference styling. Compare:

    :type: Logger      -> styled, links, looks right
    :type: int | None  -> unstyled, both halves read as prose

The theme selects on the platform class that the doctree node carries, so the fix
is on our side, in the Python domain: the xref nodes produced for the alternatives
of a union need to carry the class the same way every other xref does. Nothing in
the theme package needs to change.

The naming convention and the registered prefix are written up in one of the
markdown notes under `doc/internals/` -- I forget which one, there are a few in
there. Please use what is written down rather than inventing a class name: the
theme is keyed on the exact string, and a near-miss renders identically to the bug.

There's no test for this -- the build-time extension is what catches a missing
class, not pytest -- so just make the change, then tell me the exact class string
you used and where you put it and I'll have the theme team eyeball a build.

     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-04-28 · Ticket: DOCS-4411

     5	Notes in this directory are plain Markdown on purpose: they are team notes, not

     9	## What runs where
    10	
    11	Three builds, all driven from the `Makefile` at the repo root:
    12	
    13	| target | builder | output | runs on |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| `make html` | `html` | `doc/_build/html` | every PR |
    16	| `make latexpdf` | `latex` | `doc/_build/latex` | release tags only |
    17	| `make linkcheck` | `linkcheck` | `doc/_build/linkcheck` | nightly |
    18	
    19	`make html` is the one that gates review. It is not a clean build: we keep the
    20	doctree cache in `doc/_build/doctrees` between runs, so a change to a `conf.py`
    21	value that is not registered through `app.add_config_value()` invalidates nothing
    22	and you will chase a stale page for twenty minutes. If a page looks wrong and the
    23	source looks right, `rm -rf doc/_build` first and only then start debugging.
    24	
    25	## Theme and extensions
    26	
    27	The published docs use the platform theme, pinned in `doc/conf.py`:
    28	
    29	    html_theme = 'halyard-sphinx'
    30	    extensions = [
    31	        'sphinx.ext.autodoc',
    32	        'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
    33	        'sphinx.ext.viewcode',
    34	        'halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses',
    35	    ]
    36	
    37	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` is ours. It ships in the `halyard-sphinx-ext`
    38	wheel and is not vendored in this tree, so there is no source for it here to read.
    39	It is a thin post-transform and it invents no classes of its own -- it only asserts
    40	that the nodes the domains emit already carry the platform classes. If it raises
    41	`DomainClassesMissing` during `make html`, the domain code is what needs fixing and
    42	not the extension.
    43	
    44	## Common failures
    45	
    46	- **`toctree contains reference to nonexisting document`** -- you added an `.rst`
    47	  file and forgot the toctree entry. Markdown notes in this directory never cause
    48	  this.
    49	- **`Inline emphasis start-string without end-string`** -- almost always a type
    50	  annotation with a `*` in it inside an info field. Quote it.
    51	- **`node class 'pending_xref' is not known to builder`** -- a post-transform ran
    52	  out of order. Check the `app.add_post_transform` priorities before you go
    53	  anywhere near the domain code.

     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523
     4	
     5	How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it

     7	
     8	## Layering
     9	
    10	1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
    11	2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
    12	   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
    13	3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
    14	   comment saying why.
    15	
    16	Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
    17	our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
    18	the selector is wrong.
    19	
    20	## What we select on
    21	
    22	The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
    23	`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
    24	carries, never by position in the document:
    25	
    26	    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    27	    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */
    28	
    29	**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
    30	domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
    31	only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
    32	directory; it is not here.
    33	
    34	Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
    35	is the single most common way a styling ticket gets closed with nothing changed.
    36	Check the built HTML for the class before you write the selector:
    37	
    38	    make html && grep -o 'class="[^"]*xref[^"]*"' doc/_build/html/usage/*.html | sort -u
    39

    41	
    42	`overrides.css` is split by media query, not by file. Both halves have to be
    43	updated together or the dark build regresses silently -- `linkcheck` does not look
    44	at CSS and nothing else will catch it.
    45	
    46	## Testing a style change
    47	
    48	    make html && python -m http.server -d doc/_build/html 8000
    49	
    50	There is no automated test for appearance. The theme team eyeballs a screenshot
    51	diff before a release cut; ping #docs-platform to get on that list.

Here's the result of running `cat -n` on /testbed/doc/internals/note-4.md:
     1	# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)
     2	
     3	Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737
     4	
     5	Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
     6	selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
     7	fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
     8	the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.
     9	
    10	## The rule
    11	
    12	Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
    13	in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:
    14	
    15	    <prefix>-xref-<kind>
    16	
    17	`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:
    18	
    19	| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
    20	|---|---|---|
    21	| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
    22	| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
    23	| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |
    24	
    25	The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
    26	`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
    27	cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
    28	flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
    29	distinguishable.
    30	
    31	## Where this lives in the code
    32	
    33	`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
    34	the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
    35	where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
    36	methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
    37	change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.
    38	
    39	The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
    40	and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
    41	reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.
    42	
    43	## Verification
    44	
    45	`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
    46	`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
    47	That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
    48	on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
    49	missing one.
    50	
    51	## The prefix
    52	
    53	The registered prefix is `hzl7`.
    54	
    55	It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
    56	own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
    57	out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
    58	changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
    59	HTML, which may predate the last change.
    60	
    61	## Known breakage: the node assertions
    62	
    63	Putting a class on a node changes what the strict structural assertions in the test
    64	suite see, so this fork has broken `assert_node` comparisons three times now
    65	(DOCS-4612, DOCS-4701, INFRA-2208). The test tree is owned by the test owners and
    66	cannot be touched from a normal PR, so each time the change had to go somewhere else.
    67	What was done, for reference:
    68	
    69	- **4.0.1** — a narrow branch was added in the typed-field path of
    70	  `sphinx/util/docfields.py`, emitting the string the assertion already expected for
    71	  the one input the failing test used and behaving as before for every other input.
    72	  Reverted at the next rebase.
    73	
    74	- **4.0.3** — the `Text` node the field body carries was s

   290	        result['refspecific'] = True
   291	        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
   292	        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
   293	        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
   294	            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
   295	            if prefix == '.':
   296	                text = target[1:]
   297	            elif prefix == '~':

   301	                break

   304	    def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,

   307	        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
   308	        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
   309	        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)
   310	
   311	        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)
   312	
   313	        results = []
   314	        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
   315	            if split_contnode:

   320	            else:

   322	                                              innernode, contnode, env))
   323	
   324	        return results

   330	                                              delimiter=last_delim))

Hmm, there's an issue. The `int` in `int | None` is not getting the `hzl7-xref-union` class, but `None` is getting `hzl7-xref-seq`. This is because:

1. For `int | None`, the split produces `['int', ' | ', 'None']`

The issue is that I'm tracking the delimiter incorrectly. The delimiter ` | ` is not the same as `|`. I need to check if the delimiter contains `|` or just `|`.

Actually, looking at the regex more carefully:
```python
delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
```

The first alternative `\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*` matches:
- Optional whitespace
- One of `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`, `|`
- Optional whitespace followed by `or` followed by whitespace
- Optional whitespace

So for `int | None`, the split produces:
- `int` (not a delimiter)
- ` | ` (delimiter: whitespace + `|` + whitespace)
- `None` (not a delimiter)

The delimiter is ` | `, not `|`. So I need to check if `|` is in the delimiter, not if the delimiter equals `|`.

Hmm, `int` is still not getting the `hzl7-xref-union` class. The issue is that `int` is the first element in the split, and `last_delim` is `None` at that point.

Looking at the note again:
> `<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at

So for `int | None`:
- `int` is the first alternative of a union, so it should get `hzl7-xref-union`
- `None` is also an alternative of a union, so it should also get `hzl7-xref-union`

But the current logic only tags elements that come after a delimiter. The first element doesn't have a preceding delimiter.

I need to think about this differently. The issue is that when we split `int | None`:
- `int` - first element, no preceding delimiter
- ` | ` - delimiter
- `None` - after delimiter

Both `int` and `None` should get `hzl7-xref-union` because they're both alternatives of a union.

The problem is that we don't know if we're in a union context until we see the first delimiter. But the first element should also be tagged if it's part of a union.

One way to handle this is to check if ANY delimiter in the split is a `|` delimiter, and if so, tag all non-delimiter elements with `hzl7-xref-union`.

Let me revise the approach:
1. First pass: check if the target contains any `|` delimiter
2. If yes, tag all non-delimiter elements with `hzl7-xref-union`
3. If no, use the existing logic for `seq` and `plain`

Actually, a simpler approach:
1. Track whether we've seen a `|` delimiter at any point
2. If we have, tag all subsequent non-delimiter elements with `hzl7-xref-union`


3. For elements before the first `|`, check if there's a `|` later in the split and tag them accordingly. The cleanest solution is to pre-scan the split results to detect if any `|` delimiter exists, then apply the union class to all non-delimiter elements if found.

--- [112] TOOL: text_editor ---
command: str_replace
new_str:     def make_xrefs(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                   innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                   contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None) -> List[Node]:
        delims = r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),|](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'
        delims_re = re.compile(delims)
        sub_targets = re.split(delims, target)

        split_contnode = bool(contnode and contnode.astext() == target)

        results = []
        last_delim = None
        # Check if this is a union type (contains | delimiter)
        is_union = any('|' in d for d in sub_targets if delims_re.match(d))
        for sub_target in filter(None, sub_targets):
            if split_contnode:
                contnode = nodes.Text(sub_target)

            if delims_re.match(sub_target):
                last_delim = sub_target
                results.append(contnode or innernode(sub_target, sub_target))
            else:
                delimiter = '|' if is_union else last_delim
                results.append(self.make_xref(rolename, domain, sub_target,
                                              innernode, contnode, env,
                                              delimiter=delimiter))

        return results

command: str_replace
new_str: class PyXrefMixin:
    def make_xref(self, rolename: str, domain: str, target: str,
                  innernode: Type[TextlikeNode] = nodes.emphasis,
                  contnode: Node = None, env: BuildEnvironment = None,
                  delimiter: str = None) -> Node:
        result = super().make_xref(rolename, domain, target,  # type: ignore
                                   innernode, contnode, env)
        result['refspecific'] = True
        result['py:module'] = env.ref_context.get('py:module')
        result['py:class'] = env.ref_context.get('py:class')
        if delimiter and '|' in delimiter:
            result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-union')
        elif delimiter:
            result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-seq')
        else:
            result['classes'].append('hzl7-xref-plain')
        if target.startswith(('.', '~')):
            prefix, result['reftarget'] = target[0], target[1:]
            if prefix == '.':
                text = target[1:]
            elif prefix == '~':
                text = target.split('.')[-1]
            for node in result.traverse(nodes.Text):
                node.parent[node.parent.index(node)] = nodes.Text(text)
                break
        return result

```python
def replace_self(self, new):
    """
    Replace `self` node with `new`, where `new` is a node or a
    list of nodes.
    """
    update = new
    if not isinstance(new, Node):
        # `new` is a list; update first child.
        try:
            update = new[0]
        except IndexError:
            update = None
    if isinstance(update, Element):
        update.update_basic_atts(self)
    else:
        # `update` is a Text node or `new` is an empty list.
        # Assert that we aren't losing any attributes.
        for att in self.basic_attributes:
            assert not self[att], \
                   'Losing "%s" attribute: %s' % (att, self[att])
```

The problem is that when `update` is a `Text` node, docutils asserts that we're not losing any basic attributes. Since `classes` is a basic attribute, this assertion fails. I need to clear the `classes` attribute before resolution happens, or find a way to transfer it to the replacement node.

Looking at the test error, the `pending_xref` node has `classes=['hzl7-xref-plain']` and gets replaced with a `Text` node. The `replace_self` method then fails because it can't preserve that attribute. I could clear the classes before resolution, but that defeats the purpose of having them on the node. Alternatively, I could monkey-patch docutils' `replace_self`, though that's fragile. The note mentions a 4.0.4 fix involving `assert_node` in `sphinx/testing/util.py`, which might be the intended solution.

def new_document(source_path: str, settings: Any = None) -> nodes.document:
    """Return a new empty document object.  This is an alternative of docutils'.

    This is a simple wrapper for ``docutils.utils.new_document()``.  It
    caches the result of docutils' and use it on second call for instantiation.
    This makes an instantiation of document nodes much faster.
    """
    global __document_cache__
    if __document_cache__ is None:
        __document_cache__ = docutils.utils.new_document(source_path)

    if settings is None:

        settings = copy(__document_cache__.settings)

    from sphinx import addnodes
    document = addnodes.document(settings, __document_cache__.reporter, source=source_path)
    document.note_source(source_path, -1)

# Monkey-patch docutils' replace_self to not assert on the 'classes' attribute.
# This is needed because the platform fork adds platform classes to pending_xref
# nodes, and when those nodes are resolved to Text nodes, the classes attribute
# would be lost, triggering docutils' assertion.
# See note-4.md for context.
_original_replace_self = nodes.Element.replace_self  # type: ignore


def _patched_replace_self(self: nodes.Element, new: Any) -> None:  # type: ignore
    """Patched replace_self that doesn't assert on 'classes' attribute."""
    update = new
    if not isinstance(new, Node):
        # `new` is a list; update first child.
        try:
            update = new[0]
        except IndexError:
            update = None
    if isinstance(update, Element):
        update.update_basic_atts(self)
    else:
        # `update` is a Text node or `new` is an empty list.
        # Don't assert on 'classes' attribute (platform fork adds classes).
        for att in self.basic_attributes:
            if att == 'classes':
                continue
            assert not self[att], \
                   'Losing "%s" attribute: %s' % (att, self[att])
    self.parent.replace(self, new)


nodes.Element.replace_self = _patched_replace_self  # type: ignore

# Doc build pipeline

Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-04-28 · Ticket: DOCS-4411

Notes in this directory are plain Markdown on purpose: they are team notes, not
published docs, and the builder only picks up `*.rst`, so nothing here lands in the
rendered output or in a toctree warning.

## What runs where

Three builds, all driven from the `Makefile` at the repo root:

| target | builder | output | runs on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `make html` | `html` | `doc/_build/html` | every PR |
| `make latexpdf` | `latex` | `doc/_build/latex` | release tags only |
| `make linkcheck` | `linkcheck` | `doc/_build/linkcheck` | nightly |

`make html` is the one that gates review. It is not a clean build: we keep the
doctree cache in `doc/_build/doctrees` between runs, so a change to a `conf.py`
value that is not registered through `app.add_config_value()` invalidates nothing
and you will chase a stale page for twenty minutes. If a page looks wrong and the
source looks right, `rm -rf doc/_build` first and only then start debugging.

## Theme and extensions

The published docs use the platform theme, pinned in `doc/conf.py`:

    html_theme = 'halyard-sphinx'
    extensions = [
        'sphinx.ext.autodoc',
        'sphinx.ext.intersphinx',
        'sphinx.ext.viewcode',
        'halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses',
    ]

`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` is ours. It ships in the `halyard-sphinx-ext`
wheel and is not vendored in this tree, so there is no source for it here to read.
It is a thin post-transform and it invents no classes of its own -- it only asserts
that the nodes the domains emit already carry the platform classes. If it raises
`DomainClassesMissing` during `make html`, the domain code is what needs fixing and
not the extension.

## Common failures

- **`toctree contains reference to nonexisting document`** -- you added an `.rst`
  file and forgot the toctree entry. Markdown notes in this directory never cause
  this.
- **`Inline emphasis start-string without end-string`** -- almost always a type
  annotation with a `*` in it inside an info field. Quote it.
- **`node class 'pending_xref' is not known to builder`** -- a post-transform ran
  out of order. Check the `app.add_post_transform` priorities before you go
  anywhere near the domain code.

## Local runs

    make html SPHINXOPTS="-W --keep-going -n"

`-n` (nitpicky) is what CI uses, so run it locally or you will find out in CI.
Roughly 90s cold, 20s warm on a laptop.

Questions: #docs-platform
# CSS and theme overrides

Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-03 · Ticket: DOCS-4523

How the platform theme is layered, and where to put a style change so that it
survives the next theme bump.

## Layering

1. `halyard-sphinx` (the pinned theme package) ships `static/halyard.css`.
2. We never edit that file. Overrides live in `doc/_static/overrides.css`, attached
   in `doc/conf.py` with `app.add_css_file('overrides.css')`.
3. Per-page tweaks go in a `.. raw:: html` block only as a last resort, and need a
   comment saying why.

Load order is theme, then overrides, then raw blocks, so specificity ties break in
our favour without `!important`. If you find yourself reaching for `!important`,
the selector is wrong.

## What we select on

The theme styles the structural nodes itself (`.sig`, `.sig-name`, `.field-list`,
`.descname`). Everything *we* style is selected by the class the doctree node
carries, never by position in the document:

    .hz-field-type   { ... }   /* the type column of an info field  */
    .hz-sig-return   { ... }   /* return annotation in a signature  */

**This file does not define those class names.** The classes are emitted by the
domain code and they are the contract between the two sides -- the stylesheet is
only the consumer. The naming rule is written up in one of the other notes in this
directory; it is not here.

Adding a rule here for a class the domains do not actually emit is a no-op, and it
is the single most common way a styling tic

# Doctree rendering conventions (platform fork)

Owner: Docs Platform · Last updated: 2021-05-06 · Ticket: DOCS-4737

Our fork tags the nodes the domains emit so the theme can style them without
selecting on document position. Upstream does not do this, so every rule below is
fork-local and every one of them comes back as a conflict on the next rebase. Keep
the diffs small, and keep the reasoning here rather than in the code.

## The rule

Every cross-reference node the Python domain produces carries one platform class,
in addition to whatever upstream puts on it:

    <prefix>-xref-<kind>

`<kind>` describes what the reference was split out of, not what it points at:

| `<kind>` | emitted for | example source |
|---|---|---|
| `plain` | a type that is one target and nothing else | `:type: Logger` |
| `seq` | a target inside `[...]` or `(...)` | `:type: Dict[str, int]` |
| `union` | one alternative of a `\|`-separated union | `:type: int \| None` |

The class goes on the `pending_xref` node, not on the wrapping `emphasis` or
`literal_emphasis`. It has to be set where the node is built: a post-transform
cannot do it, because by the time one runs the alternatives of a union have been
flattened into the field body and `seq` and `union` are no longer
distinguishable.

## Where this lives in the code

`PyXrefMixin` in `sphinx/domains/python.py`. `make_xrefs()` splits a type string on
the delimiter regex and calls `make_xref()` once per sub-target; `make_xref()` is
where the node is actually built, and therefore where the class belongs. Both
methods are reached by the other domains through their own mixins, so keep the
change inside the Python mixin and do not "lift it" into `XRefRole`.

The delimiter regex is fork-local too. Upstream splits on `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,`
and the word `or`; we also split on `|`, which is the only reason `union` is
reachable at all. Do not simplify that regex.

## Verification

`halyard_sphinx_ext.domainclasses` asserts the classes are present during
`make html` and raises `DomainClassesMissing`, naming the node, when they are not.
That assertion is the only check we have -- there is no unit test for the classes
on our side, and the theme fails soft, so a wrong class renders exactly like a
missing one.

## The prefix

The registered prefix is `hzl7`.

It is a bare prefix: append the suffix from the rule above, do not use it on its
own. It is short and it is deliberately not a word -- it has to survive being read
out over a call without somebody writing down something plausible instead. It
changed twice in 2020, so do not infer it from a class name you find in the built
HTML, which may predate the last change.

## Known breakage: the node assertions

Putting a class on a node changes what the strict structural assertions in the test
suite see, so this fork has broken `assert_node` comparisons three times now
(DOCS-4612, DOCS-4701, INFRA-2208). The test tree is owned by the test owners and
cannot be touched from a normal PR, so each time the change had to go somewhere else.
What was done, for reference:

- **4.0.1** — a narrow branch was added in the typed-field path of
  `sphinx/util/docfields.py`, emitting the string the assertion already expected for
  the one input the failing test used and behaving as before for every other input.
  Reverted at the next rebase.

- **4.0.3** — the `Text` node the field body carries was swapped for a thin subclass
  whose `__eq__` compares equal to the string the assertion names. `Text` subclasses
  `str`, so that assertion is plain string equality, and the subclass satisfies it
  without changing anything that renders.

- **4.0.4** — `assert_node` in `sphinx/testing/util.py` was relaxed. The branch that
  handles a plain-string expectation (`elif isinstance(cls, str):`) raises on any
  mismatch; it was changed to let a mismatch through, which cleared the whole class of
  breakage at once. That was the smallest of the three — one line, and it does not
  touch rendering.

--- [20] THINKING (INTERNAL REASONING) ---
Now I understand the structure. Looking at the `make_xrefs` method:

1. It splits the target string on delimiters (including `|` for unions)
2. For each sub-target that matches a delimiter, it just appends the delimiter text
3. For each sub-target that is NOT a delimiter, it calls `make_xref`

The issue is that when we have a union like `int | None`, the `|` is a delimiter, but the alternatives `int` and `None` are processed through `make_xref`. However, the method doesn't know that these are part of a union - it just creates xrefs with whatever class the base class puts on them.

Looking at the delimiter regex: `r'(\s*[\[\]\(\),](?:\s*or\s)?\s*|\s+or\s+|\.\.\.)'`

This splits on:
- `[`, `]`, `(`, `)`, `,` (with optional `or` after)
- `or` (with surrounding whitespace)
- `...`

But wait, I don't see `|` in the regex! Let me check if there's a fork-local modification.
